# Triage: 03-node-cli-tool (Commander.js, treated as a fresh PR)

**Top-line:** Block merge. Three high-severity structural findings + eight broken tests (zero assertions in a critical error-handling suite) make this unsafe to land as-is on an empty baseline. Most remaining mediums are real but addressable post-merge.

## BLOCK (must fix before merge)

| ID | Charge | Sev / agent_risk | Why blocking |
|---|---|---|---|
| crime_00001 | God File `lib/command.js` | high / 0.63 | 2179 lines, 7.3× threshold, 150 top-level fns. For *new* code this is a non-starter — every future edit collides with code the next agent won't load into context. |
| crime_00003 | God Function `_executeSubCommand` | high / 0.62 | 120-line orchestrator inside the God File. Compounds with #1. |
| crime_00019–26 | 8× weak_test_signal in `tests/command.exitOverride.test.js` | medium / 0.46 each | **Zero** expect/assert calls in tests named "...then throw CommanderError". These are the safety net for the exitOverride contract; if they don't assert, the contract is unprotected. Either the suite was committed mid-refactor or wraps assertions in a way the detector can't see — verify before merge. |
| crime_00027–34 | 8× weak_test_signal in `tests/ts-imports.test.ts` | medium / 0.46 each | Same pattern: zero asserts in tests that supposedly verify type exports. If they only do `import { X }`, they validate compile, which is fine — but the test names imply more. Delete or assert. |

## WARN (land it, file follow-ups)

| ID(s) | Charge | Sev / agent_risk | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| crime_00002 | God File `typings/index.d.ts` (891 lines) | high / 0.63 | `.d.ts` files legitimately get large; downgrade in priority but split when a public-API boundary changes. |
| crime_00008, 00010, 00011 | God Functions `parseOptions` (115), `_parseCommand` (80), `addOption` (69) | medium / 0.52–0.53 | Extract helpers in a follow-up; all live in the God File so they'll fall out of that split. |
| crime_00014, 00015, 00018 | God Files `index.test-d.ts` (480), `help.js` (461), `option.js` (326) | medium / 0.50–0.51 | Near threshold; track but don't block. |
| crime_00005, 00006 | Duplicate block `choices` between `lib/argument.js` and `lib/option.js` | medium / 0.54 | Real domain coupling — same validation policy in two classes. Extract shared helper next refactor. |
| crime_00004 | Duplicate `myParseInt` across two examples files | medium / 0.54 | Examples — fine to leave duplicated for didactic clarity. Borderline warn/ignore. |
| crime_00007 | Hardcoded `localhost:1234` in `lib/command.js:2152` | medium / 0.53 | Likely inside a JSDoc example string in this library — verify; if real runtime code, block. |
| crime_00012, 00013 | Unprefixed booleans in `command.js` (9) and `index.d.ts` (19) | medium / 0.52 | Public API names — renaming would break consumers. Add to `allowedNames` allowlist rather than rename. |
| crime_00036 | Sync I/O (`existsSync`, `realpathSync`) in `_executeSubCommand` | low / 0.44 | Subcommand resolution at startup — sync is intentional and idiomatic here. Suppress with rationale. |

## IGNORE (noise on this codebase)

| ID(s) | Charge | Sev / agent_risk | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| crime_00009 | "PORT" magic literal across examples + typings test | medium / 0.52 | The literal *is* the example payload — that's the point of `examples/`. False positive in non-domain tier. |
| crime_00016, 00017 | Docs-code drift in `zh-CN` translations | low / 0.51 | Translation maintenance, not agent risk. Fix opportunistically. |
| crime_00035, 00039–42 | Large describe-callback bodies in test files | low–medium / 0.34–0.45 | Test organization preference; Commander's flat-describe style is consistent and readable. |
| crime_00037 | Booleans `mandatory`/`hide` in `lib/option.js` | low / 0.42 | Public API surface — see #12/#13 rationale. |
| crime_00038 | Commented-out spawn snippet in signals test | low / 0.36 | One-off; delete on touch. |
| crime_00043–51 | Weak-matcher tests in `copySettings.test.js`, `variadic.test.js` | low / 0.34 | "2 weak matchers" usually means `toEqual(false)` / `toBeTruthy()` — adequate for property-copy assertions. |
| crime_00052 | Logic-in-comments in signals test | low / 0.31 | Historical context note, not a hidden rule. |

## Justification frame

- **agent_risk ≥ 0.60** all came in as high severity and got `block` — they describe code where an agent edit is most likely to introduce a regression (large surfaces, mixed responsibilities).
- **agent_risk 0.45–0.55** are the gray zone — blocked only when paired with a *correctness* signal (zero-assertion tests). Otherwise warned.
- **agent_risk < 0.45** are nearly all ignored unless they cluster on a single file (they don't here).
- The score that tipped the test findings into block status isn't `agent_risk` itself (0.46 is medium) but the *category*: a test with zero asserts is a false-positive safety net, which is worse than no test at all.
